== README.md
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
== migrations/001_create_users.sql
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));
== schema.sql
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

arguments.command:
cd "$PWD" && cat > migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql <<'EOF'
-- migration 003: drop notes (no longer used)
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
EOF
cat > schema.sql <<'EOF'
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
EOF
rm -f /tmp/t.db; for m in migrations/*.sql; do sqlite3 /tmp/t.db < $m || echo FAIL $m; done; sqlite3 /tmp/t.db .schema; sqlite3 --version

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop notes (no longer used)
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also took `notes` out of `schema.sql` so it still matches the migrations. I ran all three migrations on a scratch SQLite database (version 3.51) and the resulting schema matches `schema.sql`. Nothing is committed yet.

**Before you merge, be aware:**
- **The data is gone for good once this runs.** The README says the deploy job applies migrations automatically, and production has 48,000 rows in `users`. Any values in `notes` will be deleted with no way to get them back. If there's any chance you'll want them later, take a backup or export first.
- **Check the production SQLite version.** `DROP COLUMN` only works in SQLite 3.35 or newer. On older versions this migration will fail.

This repo has no application code, so I couldn't confirm that nothing still reads or writes `notes`. Anything that does will break after the migration runs.
